A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain 25 pages, including appendices A–H. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and landscape appendix examples.

before.justification: v2 reports original hallucination detection, regression, transfer, and perturbation results on PHOENIX-2014T and CSL-Daily, plus ablations and qualitative analyses in appendices G–H.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and the appendices, including the numerical comparisons and prompt-injection examples.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same clean, no-video, and mismatched-video passes, reliability signals, token fusion, sentence pooling, and META combination.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate PHOENIX-2014T and CSL-Daily with the same translation tasks, visual perturbations, and adversarial-prefix scenarios. No evaluated dataset, language, domain, or scenario changes.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain confidence, perplexity, and token-entropy baselines alongside Grounding and META. SpaMo and TwoStream-SLT remain the evaluated translation systems; comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix F retain identical evaluation settings, including CHAIR-based labels, the 0.5 detection threshold, metrics, calibration, and language-specific preprocessing. Appendix perturbation settings and beam/greedy prompt-injection procedures also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The transfer analyses, visual degradation tests, feature-weight and pooling comparisons, raw-probability analysis, and qualitative translation and prompt-injection cases are identical in the main text and appendices E–H.

E5.justification: Tables 3–4 retain their statement that values are means over runs, and Figure 7 retains its median and interquartile-range display. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-reporting information changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 1 reports identical CSL-GF Grounding AUC/AP/ACC values of 0.951/0.998/0.970. Appendix Tables 3–8 and all result figures also match.

T1.justification: The reliability definitions and equations are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same assumptions A1–A4, Proposition 1, proof, and continuous variant.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about detecting SLT hallucinations through visual grounding, complementing text-only signals, generalization, and gloss-free models' weaker visual reliance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of gloss-free hallucinations, transfer behavior, feature complementarity, and prompt susceptibility are unchanged. The qualification that reliability ranks hallucination risk rather than providing calibrated probabilities is also retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds a page-1 'Code available at' statement with a GitHub repository address, absent from v2. This supplies an implementation access location; the technical and preprocessing details in Appendix F are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and novelty positioning are unchanged, including the claim to be the first investigation of hallucination in SLT.

P1.justification: The opening footnote replaces 'Preprint. Under review.' with code-availability wording and slightly revises the correspondence label. The arXiv version/date stamp updates; body prose, terminology, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded two-line footnote shifts a few lines across pages 1–3. Figures, tables, captions, and their placement are unchanged; rendered pages 4–25 are identical.

improvement.justification: The new page-1 repository pointer provides an implementation locator absent from v2, modestly improving reproducibility documentation. Scientific content and evidence remain unchanged. The supplied PDFs do not establish the linked code's completeness or usability, so the supported benefit is limited to improved access information.
